intro: Formal ways to concede a point, however much, and the doubled subjunctive of whatever happens.
p.por más que.consejo: It goes with a verb: «por más que lo intento». A real fact takes the indicative.
p.por mucho que.consejo: It goes with a verb: «por mucho que insistas». With something future or doubtful it takes the subjunctive.
p.por muy.consejo: It always takes an adjective or adverb and then «que»: «por muy tarde que sea».
p.pese a.consejo: It takes a noun or an infinitive: «pese a la lluvia». With a conjugated verb: «pese a que».
p.si bien.consejo: It is formal and hardly heard in speech. It is always written as two words.
p.aun cuando.consejo: Here «aun» has no accent: it means «even». With an accent, «aún» means «still».
p.no obstante.consejo: It is formal. It opens a new sentence and takes a comma: «No obstante, voy a seguir».
p.con todo.consejo: It goes at the start of a sentence, with a comma: «Con todo, me alegro». It is like «aun así».
p.digan lo que digan.consejo: It repeats the verb in the subjunctive: «digan lo que digan». It is «whatever they may say».
p.pase lo que pase.consejo: The same verb twice, both in the subjunctive. It suits promises: «pase lo que pase, iré».
p.quieras o no.glosa: whether you like it or not
p.quieras o no.consejo: The subjunctive is in «tú»: «quieras». For «él» you say «quiera o no».
p.conseguir.consejo: It changes e to i in «consigo» and «consiguen», but not in «conseguimos». Like «seguir».
b1.titulo: Admitting an obstacle without giving up
b1.texto:
These connectors accept a difficulty and still keep your idea.

- **por más que / por mucho que** + verb: «por más que estudio»
- **por muy** + adjective + **que**: «por muy caro que sea»
- **pese a** + noun or infinitive: «pese a la lluvia»
- **pese a que, si bien, aun cuando** + verb
- **no obstante, con todo**: they open a new sentence

The mood depends on what you say. A real fact takes the **indicative**: por más que **estudio**, no apruebo. Something open, or brushed aside, takes the **subjunctive**: por mucho que **insistas**, no iré.
b2.f0.texto: However much I study, I can't manage to pass my driving test.
b2.f1.texto: However hard it is, you will pass it.
b2.f2.texto: My father says I should give it up.
b2.f3.texto: Nevertheless, I am going to carry on.
b2.f4.texto: Whatever they say, you keep going.
b2.f5.texto: Despite the nerves, last time I almost passed.
b2.f6.texto: Whether you like it or not, tomorrow we practise together.
b2.f7.texto: All the same, I prefer to practise in the afternoon.
b2.f8.texto: Well, whatever happens, we will celebrate.
b4.texto:
**Effort or quantity that does not change the result**:

- por más que / por mucho que + verb: «por más que estudio»
- por muy + adjective + que + verb: «por muy caro que sea»

**Mood**: a real fact, indicative («por más que estudio, no apruebo»); something open or irrelevant, subjunctive («por mucho que insistas, no iré»).

**Formulas with a repeated verb**: digan lo que digan, pase lo que pase, quieras o no.

**More formal**: pese a + noun, pese a que + verb, si bien, aun cuando, no obstante, con todo.
b4.e0.texto: However much you insist, I won't go.
b4.e1.texto: Even if it rains, we will go out.
b4.e2.texto: Although the trip is expensive, it is worth it.
b5.f0.texto: A fine rain taps the windscreen of the practice car.
b5.f1.texto: Nuria grips the steering wheel with cold hands.
b5.f2.texto: However deeply she breathes, her heart beats hard.
b5.f3.texto: The examiner notes something down in silence without looking up.
b5.f4.texto: Outside, the streets shine under a grey, wet light.
b5.f5.texto: Despite the rain, the road unfolds before her like a dark ribbon.
b5.f6.texto: Nuria turns the wheel, checks the mirror and at last breathes out.
b5.f7.texto: The car stops slowly next to the wet pavement.
b5.f8.texto: Nevertheless, her hands are still trembling on the wheel.
b5.f9.texto: Even though she does not know it, a small smile is already beginning to appear on her face.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: it is formal, written, and opens a new sentence.
b6.o1.refuerzo: It is informal, conversational; it is not the formal partner.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It is neutral. Here you want the most formal: «no obstante».
b6.pregunta: Which is the formal partner of «pero»?
b7.frase: Por mucho que ____ mañana, no iré.
b7.o0.refuerzo: That is it: something future and open takes the subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It is indicative, for a fact already happening. Tomorrow is future.
b7.o2.refuerzo: After «por mucho que» comes a conjugated verb, not the infinitive.
b7.pregunta: Tomorrow is future: choose the right mood.
b8.frase: Por más que lo intento no puedo
b8.traduccion: However hard I try, I can't
b9.frase: Por ____ caro que sea, lo compraré.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Mucho» goes with verbs or nouns, not with an adjective.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Tan… que» expresses a result, not a concession.
b9.pregunta: Which word goes before an adjective?
b11.o0.refuerzo: That is «pese a que». «Pese a» alone does not take one.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Well done: «pese a la lluvia», «pese a llegar tarde».
b11.o2.refuerzo: No: normally a noun or an infinitive follows.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Correct: the same verb twice, both in the subjunctive.
b12.o1.refuerzo: It is indicative. The formula repeats the subjunctive: «pase lo que pase».
b12.o2.refuerzo: It is future. The formula needs the subjunctive in both halves.
b12.pregunta: Repeat the verb in the same mood.
p.estudio.consejo: From «estudiar», to study. In «estudio» the io is a diphthong: es-TU-dyo.
p.consigo.consejo: From «conseguir», to achieve. The g before o stays hard: kon-SI-go.
p.difícil.consejo: The accent on «í» shows the stress: di-FI-thil, with a soft th.
p.deje.consejo: Subjunctive of «dejar». The j sounds like h: DE-he.
p.seguir.consejo: The u of «gu» is silent before i: se-GIR, with a hard g.
p.aprobé.consejo: From «aprobar», to pass an exam. The accent marks the stress: a-pro-BE.
p.practicamos.consejo: From «practicar», to practise. The c before a is k: prak-ti-KA-mos.
p.practicar.consejo: The c before a is k, and the stress is on the last syllable: prak-ti-KAR.
p.celebramos.consejo: From «celebrar», to celebrate. The c before e sounds like th in Spain.
p.insistas.consejo: Subjunctive of «insistir», to insist. Stress on SIS, and the s is clear.
p.parabrisas.consejo: It is masculine, «el parabrisas», and the same in singular and plural.
p.levantar.consejo: The v sounds like b: le-ban-TAR. Stress falls on the last syllable.
p.ante.consejo: It means «before» in the sense of in front of someone or something. Stress on AN.
p.cinta.consejo: The c before i sounds like th in Spain: THIN-ta. Stress on THIN.
p.acera.consejo: Feminine, «la acera». The c before e is th in Spain: a-THE-ra.
p.intento.consejo: From «intentar», to try. Stress on TEN: in-TEN-to.
p.compraré.consejo: Future of «comprar», to buy. The accent marks the stress on RE.
p.infinitivo.consejo: It is the base form of a verb, like «hablar». The v sounds like b.
